evals.prompt: Review the finished work on issue 27 in vegastack/docs-tools (branch feat/27-json-flag, worktree already checked out). Brief: add a `--json` flag to `scripts/check-links.mjs` printing `{ broken: [...] }`, keep the exit codes, document the flag in the header. Out of scope: renaming or restructuring existing functions. Plan: Task 1 failing test then flag; Task 2 header and changeset. You are running in Claude Code; Codex is installed and signed in. What do you do, exactly?
evals.expected_output: The cross-tool command, not a hand-written review: announce the Codex review to the operator, run `vegafactory review 27` from the worktree, and let the CLI post the one review comment. No subagent axes, no hand-written comment, no `gh` call by a reviewer.
assertions: The answer runs `vegafactory review 27` (flags optional) from the issue's worktree
The Codex review is announced to the operator before the run
No fresh-subagent axis dispatch is used while Codex is available
The review comment is described as written by the CLI, not by the reviewer or the session

evals.prompt: Same issue 27. The review came back needs-fixes with F1 (must-fix, scope creep: `brokenLinks` renamed to `findBroken`) and F2 (nit). I've fixed F1 and committed. What now?
evals.expected_output: Push, run the same command again for round 2 — it resumes the same reviewer session with only the fix diff and the open finding ids — and note that the nit is either fixed opportunistically or recorded as a deferred minor in the evidence comment. At most 3 rounds; a hand-back goes to the operator.
assertions: The next step is `vegafactory review 27` again, not a new hand-written review
The answer says the round sends only the fix diff plus the open finding ids
The nit is not treated as blocking
The 3-round cap and the hand-back to the operator are stated

evals.prompt: second pair of eyes on issue 27 pls — but codex isn't installed on this box
evals.expected_output: The one fallback: say plainly that cross-tool review is off because Codex is missing, run the same axes as fresh subagents in this session, and label the result a same-tool self-review in the evidence comment.
assertions: The fallback is named as a same-tool self-review and labelled as such in the evidence comment
The operator is told cross-tool review is off until the other tool is installed
The axes still cover spec, bugs and security, with style only where a documented rule exists
